drivingQuestion: What does the clause 'some are impure with corpse impurity but not treading' add?
outcomeNote: The clause adds measuring vessels, proven from the baraita

segments.he: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁמִּטַּמֵּא טְמֵא מֵת וְאֵין מִטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס. לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי סְאָה וְתַרְקַב.
segments.en: The mishna continues: «And there are» vessels «that become ritually impure» with «impurity imparted by a corpse but do not become ritually impure» with impurity of a zav imparted by «treading.» The Gemara asks: «What is added» by this statement? The Gemara answers: This serves «to add» a measuring vessel, e.g., the measure of «a se’a or a half-se’a [vetarkav].»

segments.he: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְהַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכְּלִי״, יָכוֹל כָּפָה סְאָה וְיָשַׁב עָלֶיהָ, אוֹ תַּרְקַב וְיָשַׁב עָלָיו, יְהֵא טָמֵא?
segments.en: «As it is taught» in a baraita: The verse states with regard to the impurity of the treading of a zav: «“And he who sits on» any «object» whereon the zav sits shall wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, and is impure until the evening” (Leviticus 15:6). One «might» have thought that if a zav «turned over» a vessel used to measure «a se’a and sat on it, or» if he turned over a vessel used to measure «a half-se’a and sat on it,» that vessel «should be» rendered «impure» as a seat upon which a zav sat.

segments.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֲשֶׁר יֵשֵׁב עָלָיו הַזָּב״ — מִי שֶׁמְיוּחָד לִישִׁיבָה, יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים לוֹ: עֲמוֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ.
segments.en: Therefore, «the verse states:» “And he who sits on any object «whereon the zav sits”» (Leviticus 15:6). The wording of the verse indicates that it is speaking of an object «that is designated for sitting,» i.e., upon which people generally sit, «excluding such» a vessel, with regard to «which we say to» someone sitting on it: «Stand up and» allow us to use it to «do our work,» i.e., to measure. This is not defined as a vessel used for sitting, as it serves another function.
